verified: edh-next-119 review (must-finish round, control changes and searches; EDHREC rank 594), by hand against the Oracle text, the ten Scryfall rulings of 2020-11-10 and the CR 2026-09-25 (723.2, 723.4, 723.5, 701.23a-d, 614.1a, 616.1, 609.4b, 611.2b checked on the media.wizards.com text). Flash was already full. 'You control your opponents while they're searching their libraries.' is the rule controlSearching (sta.edhn119.controlSearching): while an opponent of the controller searches their OWN library (with any other zone of the same search), every decision of that search names the controller (core/player-control.ts record during 'search', effects/handlers/search-control.ts), who sees their cards (CR 723.4); the newest source wins (ruling: the Agent that most recently entered). The second ability is the rule searchFoundExiled (sta.edhn119.searchFoundExiled): the cards found are exiled by the searching player as they are found, the rest of the effect happens and can't see them; the controller may play them for as long as they remain exiled (normal timing, a land needs a land play), mana as though of any color to cast them; with two sources the searching player (controlled) chooses which applies (CR 616.1, ruling). Scenarios: decidedBy and seat checks, a stated quality may find nothing, 'a card' must find one, a land exiled from 'onto the battlefield', the permission after the Agent leaves, the controller's own search and a search of another player's library untouched, four players with two Agents.

abilities.text: You control your opponents while they're searching their libraries.

While an opponent is searching their library, they exile each card they find. You may play those cards for as long as they remain exiled, and you may spend mana as though it were mana of any color to cast them.

verified: edh-next-119 review (must-finish round, control changes and searches; EDHREC rank 1838), by hand against the Oracle text, the Scryfall rulings of 2025-01-24 and the CR 2026-09-25 (723.1, 723.1a-b, 723.3-723.5, 500.7, 113.6k checked on the media.wizards.com text). The cost reduction, flying, trample and protection from instants were already full. 'When you cast this spell, ...' is a cast trigger of the spell itself that functions on the stack and resolves before the spell (CR 113.6k; the existing castSelf reading, lower/cast-self.ts); the effect is controlPlayer during 'turn' with thenExtraTurn (eff.edhn119.gainControlPlayer.nextTurn.thenExtraTurn, the two sentences joined by lower/join-edhn119.ts): the target opponent's next turn that they actually take is decided by the controller (core/player-control.ts, std-control-3's record), and as that turn ends one extra turn of that player is added directly after it (core/turn.ts#playerControlAtTurnEnd; CR 500.7). Rulings checked: the player is still the active player; a skipped turn does not count; two Emrakul effects on one turn make two extra turns; a player who loses during the controlled turn takes no extra turn. Scenarios: turn order 2 (controlled) / 3 (extra, own) / 4 (caster), the cast trigger before the spell, two effects, a player leaving the game, the plain control effect as the negative.
